design.current_state:
Orb is single-facility by construction. Verified in code on 2026-10-03.

1. There is no facility or tenant concept. None of the 153 tables has a facility column. Hospital identity is site.toml [site].name and timezone (server/services/site_config_service.py:146-160, 233-234), copied once into process env vars (:320-352). The hospital clock is one process-wide zone (server/services/hospital_time.py:33-39). There is no HFR, ABDM HIP or NABH identifier anywhere (W162). CIO_SECURITY_QUESTIONNAIRE.md 1.5 says there is no multi-tenancy.

2. Invoices. invoice_print_view builds the supplier block at print time from the site name, and address and GSTIN print "Not configured" (server/services/billing_service.py:2075-2113). The invoices DDL stores only place_of_supply and is_interstate (server/migrations.py:2040-2041), so there is no supplier snapshot. Once identity becomes editable, a reprint would change an issued GST invoice.

3. The access boundary is department only.
- users carries role and department (server/database.py:35-44).
- A patient's department is that of the latest admission (PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL, server/permissions.py:428-433). department_scope (:369-397) returns None for a blank department, which means hospital-wide.
- DEPARTMENT_REQUIRED_ROLES = doctor and nurse (:406). Pharmacist, admin and cashier are department-less by design (:398-405; migration 36; F109 recommends keeping pharmacy hospital-wide).
- enforce_patient_scope (:479-503) returns 404 and writes no audit row. require_patient_access (:663-708) writes an authorization patient_scope_denied row.
- Call counts: department_scope 79, enforce_patient_scope 55, require_patient_access 61, scope_patient_ids_sql 15, patient_in_scope 15. There are 237 FROM/JOIN patients|admissions sites across about 60 files.
- Some lanes never call a scope helper. pharmacy_routes.py (/api/pharmacy/pending :38, verify :54, reject :117) has zero scope calls, and so do flight_recorder_routes.py and audit_routes.py. vigil_service.scored_admitted_patients(department) (:823) takes the department as an argument; board_order (:808) is only a sort key.
- Sage keeps a parity-tested duplicate (_scope_sql, _patient_in_scope). Its _out_of_scope_locators (server/services/sage_service.py:1964-1987, used at :2650) deliberately reads every admitted or discharged patient's id, name and bed as the complement set.

4. User loaders. Six places build the user dict straight from SELECT * FROM users: auth.py:441 (_load_session_context), auth_routes.py:424, 646, 1362, admin_users_routes.py:180, and ws/realtime.py:196 (the socket _authenticate). Rooms are dept:{dept} or dept:__all__ (realtime.py:281-286, 368-375). There are 17 INSERT INTO users sites. Staff are created at admin_users_routes.py:311, scripts/create_admin.py:242, scripts/seed_clinical_data.py:303 (INSERT OR REPLACE, after init_db at :12) and scripts/seed_relay_chats.py:50. The rest are service, bot, bench or patient-portal accounts.

5. Patient identity.
- mrn is TEXT UNIQUE per appliance (database.py:51).
- admit_patient mints a new patient and MRN on every admission (admission_service.py:244-249; coverage :194 says there is no MPI).
- Roster import does re-admit an existing MRN when no admission is open, and it can change an open admission's department (server/services/roster_import.py:1555-1593).
- Clinical tables (vitals, risk_scores, medications, orders, clinical_documents) have no admission_id. Facility attribution through the patient is therefore exact only while all of a patient's admissions are at one facility.

6. Ingestion. _resolve_patient_id matches patients.id, then mrn, then LOWER(mrn) across the whole appliance (server/services/ingestion_service.py:101-125). PV1 supplies only the encounter id (ingestion_adapters.py:320-326). Unknown patients: vitals raise (:167-169), and observations are kept with a NULL patient_id (:1192-1200). The monitor feed is one process-global listener (config.py:482-517).

7. Masters.
- There is no departments table. The legal list comes from users.department (frontdesk_service.py:342-385), and admission canonicalises through it (admission_service.py:94-107).
- Wards and beds are free text, and ward capacity is a guess (forecast_service.py:72-131).
- OPD tokens are allocated per (date, department, doctor) (frontdesk_service.py:226-227, 558-573).
- document_number_series has series_code UNIQUE (migrations.py:2100-2113) with 10 seeded series (:1827-1838 seven, :4021 KIND, :4100-4106 INC and NABHPACK). It is looked up by code alone at billing_masters.py:673, billing_service.py:2096, payments_service.py:289 and payments_routes.py:261, and re-seeded by ensure_default_masters (billing_masters.py:735-750). There are about 13 next_document_number call sites in 7 files.
- The default tariff plan is chosen by inline SQL in 4 places (billing_masters.py:298, 384, 453, 576).

8. Lazy schema owners run after migrations on a fresh DB: ensure_frontdesk_schema (frontdesk_service.py:240) and helix_db.init_helix_db (helix_db.py:89).

9. Migrations. The runner keeps a ledger and runs each migration in its own transaction. The head is 47 (vitals_carried_from, migrations.py:5446-5495). Rebuilding an FK parent needs database._atomic_table_rebuild (database.py:1388). _rebuild_users_role_check aborts on unknown users columns (migrations.py:4773). Migrations 20 and 23 forbid FKs from administrative tables.

10. Audit.
- One SHA-256 chain over a fixed _HASH_FIELDS tuple (audit_service.py:142-147).
- Fail-closed categories: security, clinical_access, phi_access, authentication, ai_inference (:43-45).
- bound_audit_fields replaces oversized metadata with a {_truncated, original_bytes} stub before hashing (:111-137).
- audit_logs is read in 10 server files: audit_routes, flight_recorder_service (:139-381, behind audit.read), admin_routes (:366-440), admin_users_routes (:224-240), compliance_service:120, impact_service:357, consent_service:572 (patient access history), metrics_service:209, pulse_service:696, plus the chain verify in database.py.
- The category "facilities" is already used by housekeeping (housekeeping_routes.py:261).

11. Flags.
- Admin modules use _module_enabled, which defaults ON (config.py:642), published on /api/health.
- The explicit opt-in precedent is DISCHARGE_FINANCIAL_ENFORCE (config.py:866-867).
- The client caches /api/health in src/shellConfig.tsx (moduleFlags :236-320, refreshModuleFlags :328).

12. Other.
- Command Center counts are house-wide and its named list is filtered by department (command_center_service.py:76-97, 330).
- Backup copies the whole DB (scripts/backup_db.py, backup_routes.py:121-227).
- The FHIR export has no Organization resource (fhir_export_service.py:209-498).
- Ward packs are keyed by ward string (downtime_service.py:836-920).
- R025 (a) is built: the socket accepts the page's own origin (RULINGS_NEEDED:46).

Patterns to extend: the single-derivation scope helpers, site_config_service's fail-loud validation, require_module gating, billing_masters, the frontdesk covering-department resolver, and the scope-attack and ratchet test style (test_caller_named_patient_scope.py, test_patient_scope_routes.py).
design.design:
TENANCY (MS-R1, recommended (a))
- One appliance per legal entity, which is one DPDP data fiduciary, holding one or more facilities.
- facility_id lives at row level in the single SQLCipher DB. There is no tenant_id.
- Validation enforces this: every facility GSTIN must carry the same PAN (GSTIN characters 3 to 12), and facilities.pan must match when set.

WHICH LEVEL EACH TABLE SITS AT
- Group level, no column: users, patients, masters (service_items, inventory_items, vendors, payers, helix_medication_master, terminology, interactions), consent and DPDP tables, retention, model registry, audit_logs (facility goes in the hashed metadata), event_log.
- Facility level, with a column: admissions, encounters, money documents, physical resources.
- Derived, no column: vitals, risk_scores, medications, administrations, orders, documents, scribe_notes, discharge_summaries, lens, sage_*, care_bundles, escalations, allergies, problems, diet_orders, observations, messages, shadow_events. Each takes the facility of its patient's admission. The vitals and risk INSERT paths (clinical_time, carried_from) are not touched.

ATTRIBUTION INVARIANT (new after review)
Deriving the facility through the patient is exact only while all of a patients row's admissions sit at one facility. admit_patient always mints a new patient, but roster import re-admits existing MRNs and edits open admissions' departments (roster_import.py:1555-1593). Therefore:
1. While multi-facility data exists, every path that creates an admission or changes its department refuses a destination in another facility. The refusal is a 409 or a reported roster row, and it is audited.
2. ops_health counts patients with admissions at more than one facility. The count must be 0.
3. Before the OPD/MPI epic lifts rule 1, it must add encounter attribution (admission_id or encounter_id) to clinical writes. Otherwise per-facility reports, extracts, ward packs and the audit resolver would attribute F1 history to F2.

LOAD-BEARING SIMPLIFICATION (MS-R4, recommended (a))
- Department keys and ward and bed codes are unique across the appliance (case-insensitive), and each belongs to exactly one facility.
- Every ward scope compares admissions.department with users.department, so ward-scoped staff become facility-isolated without editing those call sites.
- The real work is the department-less accounts (admin, pharmacist and cashier, department-less by design per F109) and the house-wide aggregates.

ISOLATION IS KEYED ON DATA, NOT ON THE FLAG (changed after review)
- facility_service.multi_facility_data() is true when the facilities table holds more than one row, active or not. Rows are never deleted, so a closed satellite's records stay isolated.
- While it is false (every install today, Ward Record, demos, reseeds), facility_scope returns None before any lookup. Every path then runs exactly as it does today: no extra query, no audit metadata key, no change to socket rooms.
- While it is true, facility scope is enforced whatever the flag says. A flag-off restore of a two-facility backup, a restore drill under the test env, and an operator turning the flag off all keep isolation.
- The value is cached in process and refreshed every 30 s, and immediately on any facility write by this process. There is one process today (W029).
- No boot refusal depends on the flag or on blind surfaces. The only boot refusal is for a facilities table that is missing facility 1 or has it inactive, which only tampering can produce.

FLAG: ORB_MULTI_SITE (server/config.py)
- Default OFF, parsed as an explicit opt-in like DISCHARGE_FINANCIAL_ENFORCE, not through _module_enabled. Read at request time.
- It gates only growth: creating and deactivating facilities, assigning users to a facility other than 1, enterprise grants, and the facility selectors and labels in the UI.
- /api/health gains platform:{multi_site, multi_facility_data} beside modules.
- Facility 1's identity (GET and PATCH /api/facilities/1, the identity card) works with the flag OFF. W162 says the HFR half needs no ruling, and invoices print "Not configured" today. This replaces the former ruling MS-R10.

CREATE GATE
facility_service.can_create_facility() returns a list of reasons, which the Facilities panel shows. POST /api/facilities refuses unless all of these hold:
- the flag is ON;
- the actor holds a live enterprise grant;
- FACILITY_BLIND_SURFACES is empty;
- the audit facility index exists;
- facility 1 has a GSTIN;
- the PAN rule holds.
FACILITY_BLIND_SURFACES ships in multisite-1 as the sentinel "*", so no second facility can be created through the product until the sweep is finished. There is no live "stage A".

RUNTIME FENCE (backs up the create gate)
- New server/facility_fence.py maps route prefixes to the increment that owns them.
- A middleware in main.py: when multi_facility_data() is true, a fenced prefix returns 503 with the text "This screen is not available yet when more than one facility is on record", and an authorization audit row (facility_fence_blocked) is written.
- While the socket lane is fenced, department-less sockets join no house-wide room.
- The sentinel fences every PHI route except auth, health and facility identity. A facility inserted by SQL before the scope core exists therefore turns screens into 503s, not leaks.
- ops_health shows the fenced list.
- The list only shrinks: the SQL-site registry ratchet (multisite-5b) fails CI on any unclassified site, so an upgrade cannot add a blind surface to a live two-facility site.

DATA MODEL (migration numbers claimed at merge; head is 47)

A) facilities_spine (multisite-1)
- facilities: id INTEGER PK, uuid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE (2 to 12 characters, A-Z0-9), name (CHECK id=1 OR name IS NOT NULL), short_name, legal_name, address_line1, address_line2, city, district, state, state_code, pincode, phone, email, gstin, pan, hfr_id, abdm_hip_id, nabh_accreditation_no, nabh_valid_until, clinical_establishment_reg_no, timezone, audit_epoch_id INTEGER (MAX(audit_logs.id) at creation; NULL for id 1), is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at NOT NULL, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.
- Seed id 1 with code MAIN and name NULL. The display name falls back to site.toml [site].name, then "This hospital".
- departments. Multisite owns this table; adt owns wards and beds. Columns: id PK, facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE (trimmed scope key), display_name, is_active, created_at, created_by.
- departments seeding order, so the canonical spelling wins: active users.department first, then site.toml [[departments]], then admissions.department and department channels, then opd_visits if that lazy table exists. Variants in admissions are reported by ops_health and never rewritten.
- departments.facility_id is immutable once any user or admission references the department.
- user_facilities: id, user_id NOT NULL, facility_id NOT NULL, kind CHECK IN ('home','visiting'), department (NULL for home, NOT NULL for visiting), granted_by, granted_at NOT NULL, reason, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason.
- user_facilities indexes: partial UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE kind='home' AND revoked_at IS NULL; partial UNIQUE(user_id, facility_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL. Rows are never deleted. There is no backfill.
- enterprise_access_grants: id, user_id, granted_by, granted_at NOT NULL, reason NOT NULL, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason; partial UNIQUE(user_id) while live.
- ALTER patients ADD registered_facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1. ALTER admissions ADD facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.
- New indexes idx_admissions_patient_status(patient_id, status, created_at) and idx_admissions_facility_status(facility_id, status).
- Rules for this migration:
  - No REFERENCES: SQLite refuses ADD COLUMN ... REFERENCES with a non-NULL default, and migrations 20 and 23 forbid FKs from admin tables.
  - No users column, because migrations.py:4773 would abort the next role rebuild.
  - No triggers on clinical tables.
  - Every ALTER is O(1).

B) invoice_supplier_snapshot (multisite-2)
- invoices and payments gain supplier_facility_id, supplier_legal_name, supplier_address, supplier_gstin, supplier_state_code and supplier_snapshot_at. They are written once, when the number is assigned.
- Numbered documents always print from the snapshot. A NULL snapshot (issued before this change) prints the legacy block exactly as issued. Only drafts show the live identity.

C) facility_columns_encounters (multisite-4)
- facility_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 on opd_visits, appointments, surgeries, roster_import_runs and history_import_runs.
- ALTER only if the table exists. ensure_frontdesk_schema's DDL also gains the column.
- idx_opd_token_unique is not rebuilt: under MS-R4 the department implies the facility. It needs facility_id only if MS-R4 is ruled (b).

D) Admin tables
- 7a: rebuild document_number_series (it has no FK children) with facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 and UNIQUE(facility_id, series_code). All 10 seeded series land at facility 1, so ensure_default_masters' re-insert stays correct.
- 7b: facility_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 on invoices, payments, refunds, claims, patient_deposits, cash_counter_sessions, encounter_charges, stores, indents, purchase_orders, goods_receipts, housekeeping_units, biomedical_assets, kitchen_indents, nabh_incidents, nabh_evidence_exports, abdm_care_contexts, enrolled_devices, helix_inventory_lots and helix_stock_movements. The helix tables use ALTER-if-exists plus a change to helix_db's DDL.
- 7b: a nullable facility_id (NULL means the whole group) on tariff_plans, hospital_forecasts and hospital_holidays.

E) The audit facility index is not a migration
- A json_extract expression index built inside the boot transaction would be an O(N) stall on the largest encrypted table.
- New server/scripts/build_audit_facility_index.py creates idx_audit_facility ON audit_logs(json_extract(metadata_json,'$.facility_id'), timestamp) in a maintenance window, timed first on a backup_db.py copy. The create gate requires the index.

FACILITY RESOLUTION
facility_service.facility_scope_for(user) returns frozenset[int] or None. It reads only id, role and department plus in-process caches (department map, live home rows, live grants), so all six user loaders get the same answer with no edits to them.
1. No multi-facility data: None.
2. A service account or the patient role: None.
3. A live enterprise grant: None.
4. Department set: {that department's facility}. An unknown department gives frozenset(), and ops_health lists the account. A home row for a department-scoped account is refused on write, so the department is the only source.
5. Department blank: the facility of the live home row. With no row, facility 1. That makes reseeds, seed_clinical_data, create_admin and seed_relay_chats correct without edits, because each of them creates facility-1 staff. The only path that creates department-less staff at another facility is admin_users_routes, which writes the row in the same transaction. A ratchet lists the 17 INSERT INTO users sites.

SCOPE
- permissions.facility_scope(user) delegates to the resolver.
- FACILITY_PATIENT_SQL is the facility of the latest encounter: the latest admission (same ordering as PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL), otherwise registered_facility_id. multisite-4 adds OPD visits and appointments.
- scope_patient_ids_sql and patient_in_scope take a keyword facilities=.
  - Department-scoped: the latest admission's department equals the department AND its facility_id is in the set.
  - Department None: FACILITY_PATIENT_SQL in the set. This is MS-R5 (a), symmetric with ward staff, and never "any encounter ever".
- Document-keyed scope for money and queues: invoices, payments, deposits, counters, OPD visits, verify-queue items and lots filter on their own facility_id.
- enforce_patient_scope and require_patient_access compute facility scope themselves, so their 116 sites need no edit. A facility-caused denial writes a patient_scope_denied row with metadata.facility_scope in both helpers. A department-caused denial keeps today's behaviour, and facility denials cannot happen on a single facility.
- log_phi_read adds metadata.facility_scope only when multi-facility data exists.
- UserOut and /api/auth/me carry facility {id, code, name}.
- Sage changes _scope_sql and _patient_in_scope in lockstep, parity-tested on two-facility fixtures. _out_of_scope_locators limits the complement set to the caller's facilities. A name that matches only at another facility gets "no matching patient at <facility>" (MS-R13). The bed matcher is untouched (R026 is held).
- Sockets: dept:{key} is unchanged. While there is no multi-facility data, dept:__all__ is also unchanged. Once there is, department-less sockets join fac:{id}:all, enterprise sockets join grp:all, and emit_patient_vitals targets the department room, the patient's facility room and grp:all. realtime._authenticate uses the same resolver.
- admissions.facility_id is immutable. Moves across facilities are refused until MS-R3.

INGESTION (new after review)
- Once multi-facility data exists, every source is bound to a facility:
  - the MLLP feed by ORB_MONITOR_SOURCE_ID through site.toml [[facilities]].ingestion_sources;
  - REST ingestion by per-facility keys ORB_INGESTION_API_KEY_<CODE> in the operator env. The existing key stays bound to facility 1.
- _resolve_patient_id(db, raw, facility_id) matches only patients whose FACILITY_PATIENT_SQL is the source's facility. Facility MRNs from patient_identifiers are added when the OPD epic builds that table.
- An unbound source or a cross-facility match takes today's unknown-patient path, plus an ingestion_source_unbound audit row (MS-R14).
- The vitals INSERT path is untouched.

PATIENT IDENTITY (new after review)
- There is no returning-patient path today, so a satellite desk scoped to its facility would create duplicates and split the allergy list.
- multisite-17 adds a group-wide identity match for registration. It matches on name plus age or DOB, sex and phone. It returns only the id, name, age, sex, group MRN and registered facility code. Each search is audited as phi_access with a reason and is rate-limited.
- Registering a visit then brings the patient into the facility's scope.
- Merge, match quality and encounter attribution belong to the OPD/MPI epic, which is an explicit dependency.

SERVICES
- New server/services/facility_service.py: get, list, display_name, identity_block, multi_facility_data, facility_scope_for, facility_of_admission, current_facility_of_patient, department_facility, home_facility, can_create_facility, create, update and deactivate.
- facility_service validation: GSTIN format; state_code equals GSTIN[0:2]; one PAN across all facilities; code charset; timezone equals the appliance zone in v1 (MS-R8); facility 1 can never be deactivated; deactivation is refused while active admissions, open OPD visits or open counters exist.
- billing_masters:
  - default_tariff_plan(facility_id) replaces the 4 inline queries.
  - next_document_number(series_code, facility_id=1) and the four lookups by code take the facility.
  - Prefix rule, on create and on update: no prefix may equal, or be a string prefix of, another facility's prefix for the same document type, and none may match an already issued number (LIKE prefix||'%'). The existing unique indexes therefore never return a 500.
- frontdesk list_covering_departments(facility_id) and _resolve_covering_department become facility-aware.
- admission_service.resolve_admission_department checks the facility and stamps admissions.facility_id and registered_facility_id.
- command_center_service.house_snapshot(facility_ids).
- NABH indicators and the evidence export run per facility. downtime_service runs per facility.
- The FHIR export gains an Organization (with the HFR identifier) and Encounter.serviceProvider.
- audit_service gains a resolver: an explicit kwarg, then the patient (cached), then the actor, then null with facility_unresolved. It runs only when multi-facility data exists. bound_audit_fields carries facility_id into the truncation stub before hashing.
- site_config_service accepts an optional [[facilities]] array (code, downtime_mirror_dir, ingestion_sources). Unknown keys fail with the file and line. Paths stay in the operator file, never in a UI-editable column.

ROUTES: server/routes/facility_routes.py at /api/facilities
- GET "" and GET "/{id}" (facility.read) and PATCH "/{id}" (facility.manage, own facility). These work with the flag OFF for facility 1.
- POST "" and POST "/{id}/deactivate": 404 with the flag OFF, then the create gate.
- GET and POST "/{id}/departments"; GET and PUT "/{id}/document-series".
- POST /api/admin/users/{id}/facility; GET and POST /api/admin/enterprise-grants, plus POST /{id}/revoke.
- Command Center, NABH and audit routes accept ?facility= only to narrow within the caller's scope. Outside it they return 404.
- The first grant is made through scripts/grant_enterprise_access.py (needs physical access, audited).

PERMISSIONS: facility.read and facility.manage, granted to admin. roles.py is unchanged. Group reach comes from an audited per-user grant, admin-only in v1 (MS-R6). A central pharmacy (MS-R9 (b)) would need MS-R6 (b).

UI
- The AdminPanel "facilities" tab mounts a new FacilitiesPanel.tsx. The identity card is always shown; create, departments, series and price list need the flag.
- UsersPanel: a facility column, a home facility select for department-less staff, the department list filtered by facility, and a grant control.
- ClinicianShell roleLine shows the facility when there is multi-facility data.
- CommandCenter gets a facility label and a selector for enterprise users. Audit views get a facility column and filter. BillingPanel shows "Applies to" on tariffs. HelixPanel gets a facility label.
- Platform flags come from the existing /api/health refresh in shellConfig.tsx (refreshModuleFlags). There is no second fetch.
- New src/api/facilities.ts, because client.ts has other edits in progress.

AUDIT
- The facility goes into metadata_json only when there is multi-facility data. _HASH_FIELDS does not change, so the chain is not bumped and the int-versus-TEXT trap is avoided.
- Reading rule:
  - A row with metadata.facility_id belongs to that facility.
  - A row without it, whose id is at or below the smallest facilities.audit_epoch_id, is facility 1, so F1's admin keeps the whole history from before the expansion.
  - A later row without it is enterprise-only.
- Readers, all handled in multisite-11:
  - Filtered row-level: audit_routes and flight_recorder_service.
  - Filtered aggregates: admin_routes /overview, compliance_service, impact_service, and admin_users_routes last-login.
  - Appliance-level by design, no filter: metrics_service, pulse_service egress, and the chain verify, whose counts every reader sees.
  - Group-wide by design: consent_service access history (the DPDP right of the data principal).
- Events:
  - site_admin (fail-soft): facility_created, facility_updated (with a diff), facility_deactivated, document_series_updated, tariff_plan_scope_changed.
  - security (fail-closed): user_facility_assigned, user_facility_revoked, enterprise_access_granted, enterprise_access_revoked.
  - authorization: patient_scope_denied, facility_fence_blocked, cross_facility_move_refused, ingestion_source_unbound.

ACROSS FACILITIES
- Backups stay whole-appliance, so a restore rolls back every facility (MS-R12). This is stated on Data and Backups and in CIO questionnaire 1.5.
- Exports, ward packs and mirrors are per facility. A facility extract CLI supports exit.
- Command Center shows the facility view by default and the group view for enterprise users.

OTHER EPICS
- adt: multisite-1 lands first and owns departments. adt-1 creates wards and beds with facility_id and codes unique across the group. Per-facility capacity replaces WARD_CAPACITY.
- opd/MPI: required for multisite-17 and before the attribution invariant can be lifted. patient_identifiers(facility_id, id_type, value) holds legacy facility MRNs.
- medorder: the facility comes from the admission.
- grn: lots and stores per facility; vendors stay group-wide.
- lis: stamp performing_facility_id, because a central lab serving satellites is the common pattern.
- abdm: HIP and HFR per facility.

SIZE
- Full plan: 87.5 engineer-days across 23 increments.
- Go-live core, everything the create gate and the fence need plus ingestion binding and the drill (multisite-1 to 12, 15, 16, 18): 69.5 days.
- Add 3 days (multisite-17) if a satellite runs OPD.
- The coverage map's "2 to 3 weeks" covers only the schema.

REVIEW DISPOSITION
- All 20 critique points were re-checked against the code and accepted.
- Two were narrowed: consent access history stays group-wide, and the audit index becomes a maintenance step.
- The review understated one point: roster import is a live readmit and department-change path, so the attribution invariant is enforced now.

functions.function: Facility master and identity (legal name, address, GSTIN, PAN, state code)

product_rulings.question: MS-R1. Tenancy model: one appliance per legal entity with a row-level facility_id, or one appliance per facility with a federated patient index? May different legal entities ever share an appliance?
product_rulings.options: (a) Row-level facility_id, one legal entity per appliance, no tenant_id, with the PAN rule enforcing it. (b) One appliance per facility plus a federated MPI. (c) Row-level with a tenant_id for franchises.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). It is one DPDP data fiduciary, it keeps CIO questionnaire 1.5 true, and consultants get one login. facilities.uuid keeps federation possible later.

product_rulings.question: MS-R2. Once a patient is in your scope, do you see their records from encounters at other facilities in the group?
product_rulings.options: (a) The whole chart. (b) Only this facility's encounters, with allergies, active medications and problems always group-wide. (c) Only this facility's encounters. Note on cost: (b) and (c) need encounter attribution (admission_id) on about 20 clinical tables and every writer, about 10 to 15 extra days owned by the MPI epic and not in this plan. Today (c) behaves like (a) for inpatients, because each patient row has admissions at one facility.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Never filter allergies, active medications or problems by facility; hiding them is how a known anaphylaxis is missed at the second site.

product_rulings.question: MS-R3. When a patient moves between facilities (transfer, or roster import re-admission or department change), what happens to active medication orders, escalation chains, Sepsis bundles and diet orders?
product_rulings.options: (a) Discharge plus a new admission at the receiving facility, mandatory reconciliation, nothing carried silently, open chains listed for close-with-reason. (b) Carry everything across. (c) Refuse in v1.
product_rulings.recommendation: (c) until ruled, then (a), in line with the R009 recommendation. Until then every move into another facility is refused or reported and audited.

product_rulings.question: MS-R4. Must department names and ward and bed codes be unique across the group, or may two facilities both have 'ICU'?
product_rulings.options: (a) Unique across the group, each owned by one facility. (b) Duplicates allowed, with every comparison facility-qualified (this also adds facility_id to the OPD token index).
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). It isolates ward-scoped staff without touching the scope call sites, and it removes wrong-patient risk in bed-based lookups. (b) roughly doubles the estimate.

product_rulings.question: MS-R5. Which patients may a facility-bound department-less account (admin, pharmacist, cashier) open?
product_rulings.options: (a) Patients whose latest encounter is at the facility, the same rule as ward staff, plus their facility's own invoices, visits and queue items by the document's facility. (b) Anyone with any encounter, ever, at the facility. (c) An active encounter, or one within N days.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). (b) gives permanent chart access, including to a patient now admitted elsewhere. State the rule in the CIO questionnaire.

product_rulings.question: MS-R6. Who may hold group-wide (enterprise) access?
product_rulings.options: (a) Admin role only, by named audited grant. (b) Also a named group desk (a pharmacist for a central pharmacy, a cashier for a central billing office). (c) Any role.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), matching the F109 recommendation of no hospital-wide clinical accounts. (b) only if MS-R9 is ruled (b).

product_rulings.question: MS-R7. Visiting consultants at two facilities: one account with a per-session facility switch, or separate accounts?
product_rulings.options: (a) One account, one active facility per session, switch audited. (b) Separate accounts. (c) One account seeing both at once.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), built in multisite-19; (b) for the first go-live.

product_rulings.question: MS-R8. In v1, must all facilities on one appliance share one timezone and one escalation ladder?
product_rulings.options: (a) One zone and one ladder, signed by each facility's clinical lead. (b) Per-facility ladders (about 3 extra days). (c) Per-facility zones too.
product_rulings.recommendation: One zone (all Indian sites are IST). Per-facility ladders unless every clinical lead signs the shared one; a ladder that pages a role a satellite does not staff at night stalls.

product_rulings.question: MS-R9. Is pharmacy stock and the verify queue per facility, or one central pharmacy for the group? (F109 recommended keeping pharmacy hospital-wide; under (a) that means facility-wide.)
product_rulings.options: (a) Per facility. (b) Central pharmacy dispensing to all facilities. (c) Configurable.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Drug licences are per premises and stock must be where the patient is. (b) would need MS-R6 (b).

product_rulings.question: MS-R11. Patient identity across facilities: one group MRN per person, or per-facility MRNs linked to one person?
product_rulings.options: (a) One group MRN, with legacy facility MRNs kept as identifiers. (b) Per-facility MRNs with an MPI link.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Duplicates across sites split the allergy list. Matching and merge belong to the OPD/MPI epic; multisite-17 supplies the group-wide identity match.

product_rulings.question: MS-R12. Do we accept that restoring a backup rolls back every facility on the appliance?
product_rulings.options: (a) Accept and state it. (b) Build per-facility restore (not feasible in one DB).
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). State it in the CIO questionnaire and on Data and Backups.

product_rulings.question: MS-R13. When a clinician names a patient in Sage who exists only at another facility, what does Sage say?
product_rulings.options: (a) 'No patient matching that at <this facility>', which is true and discloses nothing. (b) 'A patient matching that is on record at another facility of the group', mirroring the department notice. (c) Name the facility.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Today's department notice exists so a clinician never concludes a record is missing; naming the facility in (a) keeps that distinction without turning Sage into a group-wide existence lookup.

product_rulings.question: MS-R14. In a multi-facility install, what happens to monitor or lab data from a source not bound to a facility, or whose identifier matches only a patient at another facility?
product_rulings.options: (a) File nothing and take today's unknown-patient path, with an audit row and an ops_health alert. (b) Match across the whole appliance as today. (c) File to facility 1.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). A vital filed on the wrong patient is worse than a vital held for review.

risks: Blast radius. There are 237 patient and admission SQL sites in about 60 files. A missed site is a cross-facility PHI disclosure. The SQL-site registry ratchet, the runtime fence and the leak sweep reduce this, but the sweep only finds identifiers it planted.

Data-keyed isolation means one INSERT into facilities (a script or a restore) switches the whole appliance into multi-facility mode. Until the sweep is complete, the fence turns every unfinished PHI screen into a 503. That is an outage on purpose, not a leak, and ops_health must say why.

The 'no home row means facility 1' default fails toward facility 1, not toward nothing. A future code path that creates a department-less account at another facility without the row would put it in F1 scope. The INSERT INTO users ratchet and an ops_health check guard this.

Facility attribution through the patient is exact only while every admission of a patient row is at one facility. Roster import can break that today and is guarded. The OPD/MPI epic must add encounter attribution before it allows cross-facility re-admission.
The facility and grant caches refresh every 30 s for writes made outside the process. A revoke made by a script, not the product, takes up to 30 s to apply.
Lazy schema owners (ensure_frontdesk_schema, init_helix_db) run after migrations on a fresh DB. An ALTER-only migration misses them, so their DDL changes too, with a post-boot column test.
users must never gain a column in this epic. _rebuild_users_role_check (migrations.py:4773) would abort the next role migration.
SQLite refuses ADD COLUMN ... REFERENCES with a non-NULL default. Facility integrity rests on services plus ops_health, not on foreign keys.
The audit facility index scans the largest encrypted table. It runs as a maintenance CLI, timed first on a backup copy. Facility-filtered audit reads are slow until it exists.
One appliance means one interactive LLM stream. Facilities add Sage users without adding capacity; AI ceilings are absolute.

Satellites reached over a WAN have nothing during a link outage unless their ward-pack mirror is local. R025 (a) is built, so the socket accepts the page's own origin; the remaining case is a reverse proxy that rewrites the Host header (the nginx default), which the runbook must cover.

Every audit row now resolves a facility. Uncached, that puts encrypted-SQLite reads on every PHI read, the 2026-07-30 loop-stall class. The resolver uses cached maps and runs only with multi-facility data.
admissions has no index today. Facility predicates in correlated scope subqueries would slow the board at 200 beds without the multisite-1 indexes.
Other work in progress edits the tree, git exists only since today, and the migration head is 47. Migration numbers must be claimed at merge. The suite cannot run with the shipping .env.

Size. The full plan is 87.5 engineer-days and the go-live core is 69.5, against an approved sales plan that sells a one-ward Ward Record and defers this work. The flag keeps the work inert, but it competes for the same engineer time.
DPDP. Sharing one patient record across facilities is defensible only within one data fiduciary (MS-R1). The PAN rule enforces this mechanically.
Docs drift. CIO questionnaire 1.5, the manual (assembly drift is a known trap) and the install runbook must change when facility 2 becomes possible.

A patient's department is that of the latest admission (permissions.py:428-433, PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL). department_scope (permissions.py:369-397) returns None for a blank department, which reads hospital-wide. DEPARTMENT_REQUIRED_ROLES (permissions.py:406) forces doctors and nurses to have one. Helpers: scope_patient_ids_sql :435, patient_in_scope :447, enforce_patient_scope :479, log_phi_read :506, require_patient_access :663. Call counts: department_scope( 79, enforce_patient_scope 55, require_patient_access 61, scope_patient_ids_sql 15, patient_in_scope 15, PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL 23. Sage keeps a deliberate duplicate (sage_service _scope_sql 9 uses, _patient_in_scope 7), parity-tested in tests/test_patient_scope_routes.py. There are 237 FROM/JOIN patients|admissions query sites across about 60 files. The session loader is auth._load_session_context (server/auth.py:421-441, SELECT * FROM users), so the user dict is the users row. Live sockets join dept:{dept} or dept:__all__ (server/ws/realtime.py:281-286, 368-375).

3. Masters. There is no departments table. The legal department list comes from active users.department (server/services/frontdesk_service.py:342-385), and admission canonicalises through it (server/services/admission_service.py:94-107). site.toml declares departments and wards. Wards and beds are free text, and ward capacity is a guess (server/services/forecast_service.py:72-131). Patients: one record per appliance, mrn TEXT UNIQUE (database.py:51), a random MRN when blank (admission_service.py:249). admissions has no index at all. Masters with global uniqueness: tariff_plans.code (migrations.py:1874-1888), document_number_series.series_code UNIQUE inline (migrations.py:2100-2113), stores.code (:2318), housekeeping_units unit_code (:3137), and the OPD token unique index (frontdesk_service.py:226). The default tariff plan is chosen by inline SQL in 4 places (server/services/billing_masters.py:298, 384, 453, 576).

4. Schema owners outside migrations, which run after init_db on a fresh DB: frontdesk_service.ensure_frontdesk_schema (:240, opd_visits, patient_movements) and helix_db.init_helix_db (server/services/helix_db.py:89, helix_inventory_lots, helix_stock_movements).

5. Migration framework. Ledger plus its own transaction (server/migrations.py:1-50, run_pending_migrations). Head is 47 (vitals_carried_from). An FK-parent rebuild must go through database._atomic_table_rebuild (database.py:1388), which commits early. _rebuild_users_role_check aborts on any users column it does not know (migrations.py:4773). Migrations 20 and 23 forbid FKs from administrative tables.

6. Audit. One SHA-256 chain with a fixed _HASH_FIELDS tuple (server/services/audit_service.py:142-166) and fail-closed categories (audit_service.py:43-45). Append-only triggers (database.py:452-466). Audit reads are unscoped for any audit.read holder (server/routes/audit_routes.py:11-80). Chain verify is at database.py:2002. The category name "facilities" is already used by housekeeping (housekeeping_routes.py:261).

7. Command Center. Counts are house-wide and the named list is department-filtered (server/services/command_center_service.py:76-97, 330; server/routes/command_center_routes.py:24-86).

8. Flags. Admin modules use _module_enabled (server/config.py:642), default ON, published as /api/health modules (config.py:800-835, main.py:1199-1216). The explicit opt-in precedent is DISCHARGE_FINANCIAL_ENFORCE (config.py:867). Routes gate with require_module (abdm_routes.py:109-117).

9. Backups, exports, UI. Backup is a whole-DB online backup (server/scripts/backup_db.py, server/routes/backup_routes.py:121-227). The FHIR export has no Organization resource (server/services/fhir_export_service.py:209-498). Downtime ward packs are keyed by ward string (server/services/downtime_service.py:836-920). Admin sections are in src/pages/panels/AdminPanel.tsx:22-90, the user chip roleLine is at src/pages/ClinicianShell.tsx:258, and the Command Center scope label is at src/components/command/CommandCenter.tsx:130-133, 252.

What to extend rather than replace: the single-derivation scope pattern (department_scope, plus enforce_patient_scope and require_patient_access, which take the user and so can add facility centrally), site_config_service's fail-loud validation, require_module gating, billing_masters, the frontdesk covering-department resolver, and the scope attack and ratchet test style (test_caller_named_patient_scope.py, the test_patient_scope_routes.py two-department world).
first_draft.design:
TENANCY (recommended, pending MS-R1): one appliance per legal entity (one DPDP data fiduciary), with one or more facilities. A row-level facility_id lives in the single SQLCipher DB. There is no tenant_id, so CIO questionnaire 1.5 stays true.
- Group level: patients (one record, one MRN, one allergy list).
- Facility level: encounters, money documents and physical resources.
- Clinical child rows inherit facility through the patient's admission and get no column.

LOAD-BEARING SIMPLIFICATION (pending MS-R4): department keys and ward/bed codes are unique across the whole appliance (case-insensitive), and each belongs to exactly one facility. Every PHI scope today compares admissions.department to users.department (permissions.py:428). Under that rule, every ward-scoped account is facility-isolated with no edit to the ~300 scope call sites. The real work is department-less accounts (admin, pharmacist, cashier) and house-wide aggregates.

DATA MODEL. Migration numbers are claimed at merge (head is 47). There are 5 migrations.

A) facilities_spine
- facilities: id INTEGER PK, uuid TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, code TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE CHECK(length 2-12), name TEXT CHECK(id=1 OR name IS NOT NULL), short_name, legal_name, address_line1, address_line2, city, district, state, state_code, pincode, phone, email, gstin, pan, hfr_id, abdm_hip_id, nabh_accreditation_no, nabh_valid_until, clinical_establishment_reg_no, timezone, is_active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, created_at TEXT NOT NULL, created_by, updated_at, updated_by.
- Seed id 1, code MAIN, name NULL. The display name falls back to site.toml [site].name, then "This hospital". Facility 1 can never be deactivated.
- user_facilities: id, user_id NOT NULL, facility_id NOT NULL, is_home INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, department TEXT CHECK(is_home=0 OR department IS NULL) (the home department stays on users.department, one source), granted_by, granted_at NOT NULL, reason, revoked_at, revoked_by, revoke_reason.
- user_facilities indexes: partial UNIQUE(user_id) WHERE is_home=1 AND revoked_at IS NULL, and partial UNIQUE(user_id, facility_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL. Rows are never deleted: a move is a revoke plus an insert.
- user_facilities backfill: one home row at facility 1 for every users row except SERVICE_ACCOUNT_IDS (frozen literal) and role patient.
- enterprise_access_grants: user_id, granted_by, granted_at, reason NOT NULL, revoked_*, with partial UNIQUE(user_id) live. Empty at migration.
- ALTER patients ADD registered_facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.
- ALTER admissions ADD facility_id INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.
- New indexes idx_admissions_patient_status(patient_id, status, created_at) and idx_admissions_facility_status(facility_id, status).
- Rules: no REFERENCES (SQLite refuses ADD COLUMN ... REFERENCES with a non-NULL default under foreign_keys=ON, and migration 20 forbids FKs from admin tables). No users column (migrations.py:4773 would abort the next desk-role rebuild). No triggers on clinical tables. Validity is enforced in facility_service, plus an ops_health integrity check.
- Every ALTER is O(1) in SQLite, so single-site data becomes facility 1 atomically inside the runner's transaction.

B) departments_master, only if adt-1 has not created it: departments(id, facility_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE as the scope key, display_name, is_active, created_at). Seeded from site.toml [[departments]] plus the distinct department values in users, admissions, opd_visits and department channels. adt-1's wards and beds carry facility_id from creation, and ward codes are UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE appliance-wide.

C) facility_columns_encounters
- facility_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 on opd_visits, appointments, surgeries, roster_import_runs, history_import_runs.
- Recreate idx_opd_token_unique with facility_id first.
- The lazy creators run after migrations, so the migration ALTERs only if the table exists, and frontdesk DDL gains the column.

D) facility_columns_admin
- facility_id NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 on invoices, payments, refunds, claims, patient_deposits, cash_counter_sessions, encounter_charges, stores, indents, purchase_orders, goods_receipts, housekeeping_units, biomedical_assets, kitchen_indents, nabh_incidents, nabh_evidence_exports, abdm_care_contexts, enrolled_devices, helix_inventory_lots, helix_stock_movements. The helix tables follow the same ALTER-if-exists plus helix_db DDL rule.
- Nullable facility_id (NULL means the whole group) on tariff_plans, hospital_forecasts, hospital_holidays.
- Rebuild document_number_series (no FK children, so a plain in-transaction rebuild is safe) to UNIQUE(facility_id, series_code).
- A facility 2+ series must use a prefix that no other facility uses. invoice, receipt, PO and GRN numbers then stay globally unique, and the existing unique indexes (migrations.py:2628-2691) are unchanged.

E) audit_facility_index: CREATE INDEX ON audit_logs(json_extract(metadata_json,'$.facility_id'), timestamp).

NO COLUMN, derived via the admission: vitals, risk_scores, medications, administrations, orders, documents, scribe_notes, discharge_summaries, lens, sage_*, care_bundles, escalations, allergies, problems, profiles, diet_orders, observations, messages, shadow_events. The vitals and risk INSERT paths (clinical_time, carried_from) are untouched.

GROUP LEVEL: users, patients, service_items, inventory_items, vendors, payers, policies, helix_medication_master, terminology, interactions, consent and DPDP tables, retention_policies, model_registry, audit_logs (facility in metadata), event_log.

FLAG: ORB_MULTI_SITE in server/config.py
- Default OFF, parsed as an explicit opt-in like DISCHARGE_FINANCIAL_ENFORCE. It does not use _module_enabled, which defaults ON.
- Read at request time through getattr(config, "MULTI_SITE_ENABLED").
- /api/health gains platform:{multi_site} beside modules, because module ids are shell tab ids.
- OFF means: facility_scope returns None, /api/facilities/* returns 404 (require_module), no facility key is added to audit metadata, no extra session join, no UI change, and no second facility can be created.
- Migrations still run with inert columns defaulting to 1, so Ward Record, demos and reseed behave exactly as today.
- main.py boot refusals:
  (a) flag OFF with more than one active facility, because turning the flag off would silently drop isolation;
  (b) flag ON with two or more active facilities, while any facility-bound department-less account exists and permissions.FACILITY_BLIND_SURFACES is non-empty.

SCOPE
- permissions.facility_scope(user) returns frozenset[int] or None:
  - None when the flag is off, for service accounts, and for holders of a live enterprise grant.
  - Otherwise {home facility}.
  - frozenset() for staff with no home row: they see nothing, which fails closed (unlike the blank-department convention).
- patient_in_scope, scope_patient_ids_sql and a new FACILITY_PATIENT_SQL take a keyword facilities=:
  - Department-scoped: the latest admission's department equals the department AND its facility_id is in the set (belt and braces).
  - Department None: any admission, OPD visit or appointment at the facility, or registration there.
- enforce_patient_scope and require_patient_access compute facility_scope(user) themselves, so their 116 call sites need no change. log_phi_read adds metadata.facility_scope.
- auth._load_session_context LEFT JOINs the home row and the live grant (flag ON only). UserOut gains facility {id, code, name}.
- Sage's duplicate derivation changes in lockstep (parity test).
- Socket rooms: dept:{key} is unchanged. dept:__all__ splits into fac:{id}:all and grp:all, and emit_patient_vitals targets the department room, the patient's facility room and grp:all.
- admissions.facility_id is immutable. Transfers and admissions to another facility's department are refused (409, audited) until MS-R3.

SERVICES
- New server/services/facility_service.py:
  - get, list, display_name, identity_block (invoices and prints), current_facility_of_patient, facility_of_admission, department_facility, home_facility, active_count.
  - create, update and deactivate, with validation: GSTIN format and state_code equal to GSTIN[0:2], code charset, unique codes, timezone must equal the appliance zone in v1. Deactivate is refused for id 1 and while there are active admissions, open OPD visits or open counters.
- Extended services:
  - billing_masters.default_tariff_plan(facility_id) replaces the 4 inline queries, and series numbering takes facility_id.
  - frontdesk list_covering_departments(facility_id) and _resolve_covering_department.
  - admission_service.resolve_admission_department checks the facility.
  - command_center_service.house_snapshot(facility_ids).
  - nabh_service indicators and export take a facility.
  - downtime_service mirrors per facility.
  - FHIR export adds an Organization (HFR identifier) and Encounter.serviceProvider.
  - audit_service resolves the facility into metadata.
- site.toml gains an optional [[facilities]] array (code, downtime_mirror_dir). File paths stay in the operator file, never in a column the UI can edit.

ROUTES: server/routes/facility_routes.py, /api/facilities, behind require_module
- GET "" and GET "/{id}" (facility.read; facility-bound users see their own).
- PATCH "/{id}" (facility.manage, own facility).
- POST "" and POST "/{id}/deactivate" (facility.manage plus an enterprise grant).
- GET/POST "/{id}/departments" (unless ADT owns the master).
- GET/PUT "/{id}/document-series".
- Users: POST /api/admin/users/{id}/facility; GET/POST /api/admin/enterprise-grants and POST /{id}/revoke.
- The Command Center, NABH and audit routes accept ?facility= only to narrow within the caller's scope, never to widen it.
- The first grant is made through a new server/scripts/grant_enterprise_access.py (needs physical access, audited).

PERMISSIONS: facility.read and facility.manage in permissions.py, granted to admin. roles.py is unchanged: no role string, so no users rebuild and no parity churn. Group reach is a per-user audited grant, and admin-only in v1 (MS-R6).

UI
- AdminPanel ADMIN_TABS gains "facilities" (shown only with the flag), mounting a new src/pages/panels/admin/FacilitiesPanel.tsx: list, identity, departments and wards (linking to the ADT masters), document series, default price list.
- UsersPanel: a facility column, a home facility select, and a grant control.
- The ClinicianShell roleLine appends the facility when the flag is on.
- CommandCenter.tsx: a facility label for facility-bound users; per-facility tiles and a selector for enterprise users.
- Audit views: facility column and filter.
- BillingPanel: tariff "Applies to".
- New src/api/facilities.ts (client.ts has other edits in progress) and src/lib/platformFlags.ts.
- No new shell tab, and shellConfig.tsx is unchanged.

AUDIT
- The facility goes into metadata_json, which is already hashed. _HASH_FIELDS does not change, there is no chain contract bump, and the int-versus-TEXT hashing trap is avoided.
- Resolver order: an explicit kwarg, then the patient's facility (cached), then the actor's home facility, then null with a reason. A resolver error never blocks a fail-closed write.
- There is one chain per appliance.
- Facility-bound readers see only their facility's rows. Rows with no facility are enterprise-only. Every reader still gets the verify counts.
- Events:
  - site_admin (fail-soft; not "facilities", which housekeeping already uses): facility_created, facility_updated (with a field diff), facility_deactivated, document_series_updated, tariff_plan_scope_changed.
  - security (fail-closed): user_facility_assigned, user_facility_revoked, enterprise_access_granted, enterprise_access_revoked.
  - authorization: facility_scope_denied, cross_facility_transfer_refused.

ACROSS FACILITIES
- Backups: one DB, one key, one verified backup. A restore rolls back every facility (stated on Data and Backups and in the CIO questionnaire).
- Exports: NABH evidence per facility; FHIR Organization per facility; nightly self-export and ward packs per facility folder and mirror; a facility extract CLI for exit.
- Command Center: the facility view by default, the group view for enterprise users.

OTHER EPICS
- adt: wards, beds and departments get facility_id at creation, so land multisite-1 first. Codes are unique across the group. Per-facility capacity replaces the WARD_CAPACITY guess.
- opd: facility on visits, per-facility tokens, registered_facility_id, and patient_identifiers(facility_id, id_type, value) for legacy facility MRNs under one group MRN.
- medorder: facility derived from the admission. The dispensing facility is the admission facility.
- grn: GRN into a facility store; lots carry facility; vendors stay group-wide.
- lis: keep the ordering facility (derived) and stamp performing_facility_id, because a central lab serving satellites is the common pattern. The lab worklist scopes on the performing facility.
- abdm: HIP and HFR per facility; care contexts stamped.

SIZE, stated honestly
- Full plan: 67.5 engineer-days.
- Core multi-site without the pharmacy and ruling-gated items: about 55.5 days.
- Stage A (multisite-1 to 6, ward-scoped staff isolated, department-less accounts group-wide only): about 21 days.
- The coverage map's "2 to 3 weeks" matches only the schema half.

product_rulings.question: MS-R1. Tenancy model: one appliance per legal entity with row-level facility_id, or one appliance (or process) per facility with a federated patient index? May facilities of different legal entities ever share an appliance?
product_rulings.options: (a) Row-level facility_id in one DB, one legal entity per appliance, no tenant_id. (b) One appliance or process per facility plus a federated MPI and consolidated reporting. (c) Row-level with a tenant_id for franchise chains.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). One patient record means one allergy list across the group (federation turns that into a sync problem), and consultants get one login. It keeps CIO questionnaire 1.5 true and stays within one DPDP data fiduciary. facilities.uuid keeps federation possible later.

product_rulings.question: MS-R2. Once a patient is in your scope, do you see their records from encounters at other facilities in the group?
product_rulings.options: (a) Whole chart, including other facilities' encounters. (b) Only this facility's encounters, with allergies, active medications and problems always group-wide. (c) Only this facility's encounters.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Never filter allergies, active medications or the problem list by facility. Hiding them is how a known anaphylaxis is missed at the second site.

product_rulings.question: MS-R3. When a patient moves between facilities, what happens to active medication orders, escalation chains, Sepsis bundles and diet orders?
product_rulings.options: (a) Discharge plus new admission at the receiving facility, mandatory medication reconciliation, nothing carried silently, open chains listed for close-with-reason. (b) Carry the admission and all orders across. (c) Refuse inter-facility moves in v1.
product_rulings.recommendation: (c) until ruled, then (a), consistent with the R009 recommendation on open chains. Until then the transfer route refuses a destination department in another facility.

product_rulings.question: MS-R4. Must department names and ward and bed codes be unique across the whole group (for example prefixed per site), or may two facilities both have 'ICU' and 'General Medicine'?
product_rulings.options: (a) Unique across the group, each owned by one facility. (b) Duplicate names allowed, every comparison facility-qualified.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). It isolates every ward-scoped account with no change to the ~300 scope call sites. It also removes wrong-patient risk in bed-based lookups (Sage bed locator, monitor PV1 bed mapping, Relay bed mentions). (b) roughly doubles the estimate.

product_rulings.question: MS-R5. May two facilities go live before the department-less scope sweep finishes (stage A), with every department-less account (admin, pharmacist, cashier) group-wide by explicit grant?
product_rulings.options: (a) Allow stage A for live use. (b) Stage A only for a dry run, and go live after the sweep (multisite-8 to 10). (c) No stage A.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). A group-wide pharmacist or cashier at a satellite is a least-privilege breach a CIO will find.

product_rulings.question: MS-R6. Who may hold group-wide (enterprise) access?
product_rulings.options: (a) Admin role only, by named audited grant. (b) Also a clinical role (for example a group CMO). (c) Any role.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). This matches the F109 recommendation of no hospital-wide clinical accounts.

product_rulings.question: MS-R7. Visiting consultants who work at two facilities: one account with a per-session facility switch, or a separate account per facility?
product_rulings.options: (a) One account, one active facility per session, switch audited. (b) Separate accounts. (c) One account that sees both facilities at once.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), built after stage B (multisite-17). (b) for the first go-live.

product_rulings.question: MS-R8. In v1, must all facilities on one appliance share one timezone and one escalation ladder?
product_rulings.options: (a) One zone and one ladder, signed by each facility's clinical lead. (b) Per-facility ladders (escalation_service reads per-facility tiers, about 3 extra days). (c) Per-facility zones too.
product_rulings.recommendation: One zone (all Indian sites are IST). Per-facility ladders unless each facility's clinical lead signs the shared one. A ladder that pages a role a satellite does not staff at night stalls.

product_rulings.question: MS-R9. Is pharmacy stock and the verify queue per facility, or one central pharmacy for the group?
product_rulings.options: (a) Per facility. (b) Central pharmacy dispensing to all facilities. (c) Both, configurable.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Drug licences are per premises, and stock must be where the patient is.

product_rulings.question: MS-R10. Should the hospital identity card (legal name, address, GSTIN, HFR ID) be available on single-site installs with ORB_MULTI_SITE off?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, on for everyone. (b) Only with the flag.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Invoices print 'Not configured' today, and W162 says the HFR half needs no ruling.

product_rulings.question: MS-R11. Patient identity across facilities: one group MRN per person, or per-facility MRNs linked to one person?
product_rulings.options: (a) One group MRN, with legacy facility MRNs kept as identifiers. (b) Per-facility MRNs with an MPI link.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Duplicate records across sites split the allergy list. Matching and merge belong to the OPD/MPI epic.

product_rulings.question: MS-R12. Do we accept that restoring a backup rolls back every facility on the appliance?
product_rulings.options: (a) Accept and state it. (b) Build per-facility restore (not feasible in one DB).
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). State it in the CIO questionnaire and on Data and Backups.

risks: Blast radius: 237 patient/admission query sites in about 60 files and 79 department_scope callers. A missed site in the sweep is a cross-facility PHI disclosure. The leak-sweep test, the AST ratchet and the boot refusal reduce this, but the sweep only catches identifiers it plants.
The coverage map's '2 to 3 weeks' covers only the schema half. Honest totals: 67.5 engineer-days for the full plan, about 55.5 for the core, about 21 for stage A.

MS-R4 is load-bearing. If duplicate department or ward names across facilities are allowed, every department comparison and every ward-keyed table (housekeeping, diet plans, ward packs, forecast capacity, NABH ward filters) needs a facility predicate, and the estimate roughly doubles.

Lazy schema owners (frontdesk_service.ensure_frontdesk_schema :240, helix_db.init_helix_db :89) run after migrations on a fresh DB. An ALTER-only migration silently misses them, so their DDL must change too, with a post-boot column test.
users must never gain a column in this epic. _rebuild_users_role_check aborts on unknown live columns (migrations.py:4773), which would break another epic's next role migration.
SQLite refuses ADD COLUMN ... REFERENCES with a non-NULL default under foreign_keys=ON. Facility integrity therefore rests on services plus an ops check, not FKs.
Turning the flag off after a second facility exists would silently remove isolation. The boot refusal covers this, and also (correctly) stops a flag-off restore of a multi-facility backup.
One appliance means one interactive LLM stream (llm_queue_service.py:43). Facilities add Sage users without adding capacity; AI ceilings are absolute, not per bed.

Satellites over a WAN link have nothing during a link outage unless their ward-pack mirror is local. Every facility's address must be in ORB_CORS_ORIGINS (R025 is open), or screens hang 15 to 25 seconds.
Facility resolution adds a lookup per audit row. Uncached, it puts encrypted-SQLite reads on every PHI read, the 2026-07-30 loop-stall class.
admissions has no index today. Facility predicates in correlated scope subqueries will slow the board at 200 beds unless the new indexes land in multisite-1.

DPDP: sharing one patient record across facilities is defensible only within one data fiduciary (MS-R1). A franchise of separate legal entities on one appliance would be an unconsented disclosure.
